title: TENSORMD: Accelerating Molecular Dynamics with a High-Performance Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
problem: Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) suffer from suboptimal performance when using general-purpose ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) because these frameworks are not optimized for the computational patterns and diversity of HPC+AI workloads.
motivation: While AI has enhanced HPC across scientific fields, the mismatch between ML tool optimization and the specific requirements of MLIPs leaves significant performance on the table. Standard ML frameworks cannot flexibly optimize for HPC-specific patterns, limiting the ability to achieve full hardware utilization.
method: TensorMD is a custom MLIP implementation decoupled from existing ML tools, enabling domain-specific optimizations tailored to the computational patterns of molecular dynamics. The approach identifies optimization opportunities unique to HPC+AI that general frameworks cannot exploit.
key_novelty: MLIP implementation independent of general-purpose ML frameworks, enabling hardware-aware optimizations specific to HPC molecular dynamics workloads.
contributions: Custom MLIP framework achieving 1.88x speedup over state-of-the-art MLIP (2020 Gordon Bell Prize winner) on NVIDIA A100 GPU
Demonstrated scalability to molecular dynamics simulations with 50 billion+ atoms
Evaluation on multiple supercomputer architectures with different topologies
Framework design enabling flexible optimizations not possible in standard ML tools
baselines: TensorFlow-based MLIP (2020 Gordon Bell Prize winner)
limitations: Abstract does not provide details on specific optimization techniques or memory footprint comparisons.
